name: The Rieger–Nishimura ladder
description: Rieger and Nishimura introduced this construction to study free Heyting algebras on one generator. In particular, the ladder displayed here is the Esakia dual to this algebra.

name: Fine general frame
description: K. Fine introduced this frame to study incompleteness of S4 logics. V. Shehtman later adapted it to obtain an incomplete superintuitionistic logic. It has served as a useful source of counterexamples: for instance, G. Bezhanishvili, D. Gabelaia, and M. Jibladze employed it in their negative solution to Kuznetsov’s problem for bi-Heyting algebras.

description: The dual algebras were introduced to study pre-locally tabular superintuitionistic logics and to prove that there are continuum many of them.

name: WB graph frame
description: This frame was introduced in our studies of pre-local tabularity and local tabularity, seeking a width-bounded locally tabular logic: it is not locally tabular, but all finitely generated algebras of bounded width in its variety are finite. Every finitely generated algebra in this variety is co-Hopfian.

name: Young lattice Fine frame
description: Young's lattice of partitions was introduced by A. Young in the study of integer partitions in combinatorics and number theory. This particular construction models the Fine general frame, and replaces its "kernel" (the bottom ascending part) by Young's lattice of partitions, obtaining interesting properties.
reference_blurb: This frame arose in our studies of completeness theory, seeking the extent of the Artin-gluing based completion method which was found to work for the Fine general frame.

name: Bellissima’s construction
description: Bellissima’s universal model gives a representation of the free Heyting algebra on two generators by building the "image-finite part" of the dual space. The construction is recursive, and proceeds by layers, taking into account the structure of successors and the "colors" -- the propositional variables satisfied by each point.

motivation_html:
Bellissima’s universal model gives a representation of the free Heyting algebra on two generators by building the "image-finite part" of the dual space. The construction is recursive, and proceeds by layers, taking into account the structure of successors and the "colors" -- the propositional variables satisfied by each point.

Bellissima’s universal model U(2) is the image-finite part part of X2. We begin with four maximal points, one of each colour ∅, {p}, {q}, {p,q}.

At each round we build a new layer of U(2) as follows: pick a finite antichain A from the existing model, containing at least one point from the preceding layer, and a color C which is below the color of each point in this antichain; then add a point which has A as its successors, and is colored C.

The interactive display shows the four maximal points, and a selection of 18 points (the layers grow extremely quickly -- at the third layer several hundreds or thousands of points). The color upsets in the end are given by the points sharing the colors p and q.

At the end of the construction, the poset will contain a copy of each (irreducible) 2-generated Kripke model.

name: Modified Rieger-Nishimura ladder
description: A modified Rieger-Nishimura ladder with an added point on top.
reference_blurb: This simple modification of the RN-ladder can be obtained as a p-morphic image of it, and appears recurringly in studies of completeness: in degrees of FMP, pre-local tabularity, amongst other places.

name: Countable fork
description: An order on the space omega+1, placing the compactification point on the bottom. Simple example of Priestley space which is not Esakia.

name: Countable co-fork
description: An order on the space omega+1, placing the compactification point on the top. An Esakia space which is not bi-Esakia.

name: Deleted top 2-chain space
description: The space $\omega\times 2_{\leq}$ with the upper set of isolated points deleted. Another example of a Priestley space that is not Esakia.
